author: EmuCore - Hub
title: How Rockstar fit an entire city into PlayStation 2 memory
summary: Game Maker’s Toolkit reconstructs how Grand Theft Auto III made Liberty City feel continuous inside the PlayStation 2’s 32 MB memory budget, connecting resource streaming, memory pools, fragmentation, DVD access and deliberate world design.

blocks.text: The chapter structure follows the problem from hardware constraint to game design. It first explains the 32 MB memory ceiling, then opens Rockstar’s city and streaming logic, demonstrates loading in motion, traces earlier streaming techniques, and examines pop-in, fixed pools and fragmentation. Later chapters turn to DVD seeking and the ways streets, bridges and mission routes regulate player speed. The result treats Liberty City as a coordinated memory system rather than a map that somehow happened to fit.

This is a researched reconstruction, not a profiling session captured from a retail PS2. Its unusually detailed source list includes archived Sony material, recovered GTA III files, developer recollections and technical discussions, but some implementation claims still depend on reverse-engineered code and retrospective testimony. The video is strongest when linking a visible symptom such as pop-in to a documented resource rule; exact memory totals or causal claims should still be checked against the cited source and game revision.
